bullets: Not enforceable by courts, but fundamental in governance.
The State has a duty to apply these principles when making laws.
concepts.mains: Explain how a non-justiciable directive can remain fundamental to governance, legislation and constitutional interpretation.

concepts.title: Article 40
bullets: Directs organisation of village Panchayats with powers needed for self-government.
concepts.mains: Connect village self-government with devolution, participation and the actual powers and resources of Panchayats.

concepts.title: Article 41
bullets: Within economic capacity and development, the State should secure work, education and public assistance in specified conditions of need.
concepts.mains: Assess social assistance and access to work or education while acknowledging the Article’s economic-capacity qualification.

concepts.title: Article 42
bullets: Directs just and humane working conditions and maternity relief.
concepts.mains: Connect maternity relief and humane work with women’s participation, dignity at work and enforcement capacity.

concepts.title: Article 43
bullets: Directs a living wage and conditions supporting a decent standard of life for workers.
Also promotes cottage industries on an individual or cooperative basis in rural areas.
concepts.mains: Distinguish a living wage and decent conditions from bare subsistence; connect rural livelihoods with cottage industries.

concepts.title: Article 43B
bullets: Promotes voluntary formation, autonomous functioning, democratic control and professional management of cooperative societies.
concepts.mains: Assess cooperative governance through voluntary membership, autonomy, democratic control and professional competence.

concepts.title: Article 46
bullets: Promotes educational and economic interests of weaker sections, especially Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
Directs protection against social injustice and exploitation.
concepts.mains: Connect educational and economic inclusion with protection against exploitation, particularly for SCs and STs.

concepts.title: Article 47
bullets: Improving nutrition, living standards and public health is a primary State duty.
Also addresses prohibition of intoxicating drinks and injurious drugs except for medicinal purposes.
concepts.mains: Frame public health as a governance responsibility, then consider nutrition, prevention and the design of effective public services.

concepts.title: Article 48
bullets: Directs modern and scientific organisation of agriculture and animal husbandry.
Includes preserving and improving breeds and prohibiting slaughter of cows, calves and other milch and draught cattle.
concepts.mains: Balance scientific agriculture and animal husbandry with the specific preservation and protection duties in the Article.

concepts.title: Article 49
bullets: Protects monuments, places and objects declared by parliamentary law to be of national importance from specified harm or removal.
concepts.mains: Distinguish nationally important monuments protected under Article 49 from broader heritage concerns and citizens’ cultural duties.

concepts.title: Article 51A(a)
bullets: Respect the Constitution and its ideals and institutions, the National Flag and National Anthem.
A constitutional civic duty; penalties, where applicable, arise under specific legislation.
concepts.mains: Connect respect for constitutional institutions with lawful public conduct and accountability under the Constitution.

concepts.title: Article 51A(b)
bullets: Cherish the noble ideals that inspired the national struggle for freedom.
A constitutional civic duty; penalties, where applicable, arise under specific legislation.
concepts.mains: Use freedom-struggle ideals to discuss civic education, public service and the values informing democratic citizenship.

concepts.title: Article 51A(c)
bullets: Uphold and protect India’s sovereignty, unity and integrity.
A constitutional civic duty; penalties, where applicable, arise under specific legislation.
concepts.mains: Connect unity and integrity with equal civic belonging, while retaining constitutional protections for legitimate dissent.

concepts.title: Article 51A(d)
bullets: Defend the country and render national service when called upon.
A constitutional civic duty; penalties, where applicable, arise under specific legislation.
concepts.mains: Distinguish civic responsibility for national defence from the legal arrangements governing service and mobilisation.

concepts.title: Article 51A(e)
bullets: Promote harmony across differences and renounce practices derogatory to women’s dignity.
A constitutional civic duty; penalties, where applicable, arise under specific legislation.
concepts.mains: Connect communal harmony and women’s dignity with equality, social reform and the removal of discriminatory practices.

concepts.title: Article 51A(f)
bullets: Value and preserve the rich heritage of India’s composite culture.
A constitutional civic duty; penalties, where applicable, arise under specific legislation.
concepts.mains: Use composite culture to discuss preservation of heritage alongside respect for diversity and equal citizenship.

concepts.title: Article 51A(g)
bullets: Protect and improve the natural environment and show compassion for living creatures.
A constitutional civic duty; penalties, where applicable, arise under specific legislation.
concepts.mains: Pair the citizen’s environmental responsibility with Article 48A and the rights dimension of environmental protection.

concepts.title: Article 51A(h)
bullets: Develop scientific temper, humanism, inquiry and reform.
A constitutional civic duty; penalties, where applicable, arise under specific legislation.
concepts.mains: Apply scientific temper to public reasoning, misinformation and evidence-based social reform, while respecting freedom of belief.

concepts.title: Article 51A(i)
bullets: Safeguard public property and reject violence.
A constitutional civic duty; penalties, where applicable, arise under specific legislation.
concepts.mains: Distinguish democratic protest from violence and damage to public property; examine proportionate legal responses.

concepts.title: Article 51A(j)
bullets: Strive for excellence so collective achievement continues to improve.
A constitutional civic duty; penalties, where applicable, arise under specific legislation.
concepts.mains: Connect excellence with responsible professional conduct and institutions that enable wider participation in achievement.

concepts.title: Article 51A(k)
bullets: A parent or guardian should provide educational opportunities to a child or ward aged six to fourteen.
A constitutional civic duty; penalties, where applicable, arise under specific legislation.
concepts.mains: Pair the parent or guardian’s responsibility with Article 21A, then assess practical barriers to school access and completion.

concepts.title: Habeas corpus
bullets: Requires justification for detention and enables release where detention is unlawful.
May address unlawful detention by public authorities or private persons.
concepts.mains: Match the remedy to the violation, the authority involved and the appropriate constitutional jurisdiction.
concepts.locator: Articles 32 and 226; Indian Polity, eighth edition, PDF pp. 147–148

concepts.title: Certiorari
bullets: Enables a superior court to quash an order affected by jurisdictional error or other recognised legal defects.
Often contrasted with prohibition, which restrains proceedings before an unlawful outcome.
concepts.mains: Match the remedy to the violation, the authority involved and the appropriate constitutional jurisdiction.
concepts.locator: Articles 32 and 226; Indian Polity, eighth edition, PDF pp. 147–148

concepts.title: Justice
bullets: Social justice challenges entrenched exclusion.
Economic justice addresses distribution and conditions of livelihood; political justice concerns equal civic participation.
concepts.mains: Identify the value at stake, connect it to a constitutional provision and explain the trade-off or implementation challenge.
concepts.locator: Preamble; linked provisions provide legal applications

concepts.title: Liberty
concepts.meaning: Thought, expression, belief, faith and worship
bullets: Protects individual agency and conscience.
Constitutional guarantees give particular freedoms their legal scope and limits.
concepts.mains: Identify the value at stake, connect it to a constitutional provision and explain the trade-off or implementation challenge.
concepts.locator: Preamble; linked provisions provide legal applications

concepts.title: Equality
bullets: Rejects arbitrary privilege and exclusion.
Equal opportunity may require measures addressing disadvantage.
concepts.mains: Identify the value at stake, connect it to a constitutional provision and explain the trade-off or implementation challenge.
concepts.locator: Preamble; linked provisions provide legal applications

concepts.title: Fraternity
bullets: Connects individual dignity with national unity and integrity.
Supports mutual respect across social and religious differences.
concepts.mains: Identify the value at stake, connect it to a constitutional provision and explain the trade-off or implementation challenge.
concepts.locator: Preamble; linked provisions provide legal applications

concepts.title: Objectives Resolution
concepts.meaning: Purposes debated before the constitutional text
bullets: Moved by Jawaharlal Nehru on 13 December 1946 and adopted on 22 January 1947.
Set out foundational commitments that informed the Constitution’s purposes.
concepts.mains: Assess how the process contributed to legitimacy, deliberation and accommodation, while recognising limits in representation.
concepts.locator: Indian Polity, eighth edition, PDF pp. 26–32

concepts.title: Drafting Committee
concepts.meaning: Turning deliberation into a constitutional draft
bullets: Appointed on 29 August 1947 with B.R. Ambedkar as chairman.
Worked with committee reports, constitutional advice and Assembly decisions.
concepts.mains: Assess how the process contributed to legitimacy, deliberation and accommodation, while recognising limits in representation.

concepts.title: Debate and public input
bullets: Drafts were discussed through committee work and clause-by-clause debate.
The draft was published for public comment in 1948 before further deliberation.
concepts.mains: Assess how the process contributed to legitimacy, deliberation and accommodation, while recognising limits in representation.
concepts.locator: Indian Polity, eighth edition, PDF pp. 26–32

concepts.title: Representation and its limits
bullets: Provincial members were indirectly elected; princely-state members were nominated.
The Assembly was not elected through universal adult franchise, but its deliberations sought a constitutional settlement for all citizens.
concepts.mains: Assess how the process contributed to legitimacy, deliberation and accommodation, while recognising limits in representation.

bullets: Created the Governor-General of Bengal and an executive council.
Provided for a Supreme Court at Calcutta, established in 1774.

Introduced bicameralism at the Centre while retaining a limited franchise and colonial control.
